'In classical literature, tragedy does not merely signify a catastrophic event; rather, it embodies a profound artistic examination of human limitation. 'Antibiotic resistance has quietly emerged as one of the most menacing public health perils of the twenty-first century. For nearly a century, antimicrobial agents have served as the bedrock of modern clinical medicine, transforming once-lethal bacterial infections into easily treatable conditions.
